_note: the-project-above-the-cases. A gemeente programme sits above the zaken: Omgevingswet implementatie, Sloop Kerkstraat, Verkiezingen 2027. It holds work it does not own, a team, its own tasks, a progress figure that names where it came from, and time boxes that snapshot what they showed. SLUG NOTE: the change's proposal names this object `project`, and the slug `project` is already planninq's billable delivery project. A schema slug is GLOBAL per organisation and SchemaMapper::find() matches LOWER(slug), which is the collision three Rename*SchemaSlug repair steps in this app already exist to undo, so these are named `programme*` and the two stay apart. A planninq project is reachable from here as an ordinary work item reference, so nothing is lost by the rename.

programme.title: Programme
programme.description: The work above the cases. A record with its own identity, never a tag, a label or a field on another record.

client.title: Client
client.description: The customer organisation, where there is one.

endDate.title: End
endDate.description: When it is meant to end.

progressMode.title: Progress mode
progressMode.description: Where the progress figure comes from. Administered per instance with a per-programme override, and reported WITH every figure, so a reader can tell a typed number from a derived one.

manualProgress.title: Manual progress
manualProgress.description: The percentage somebody typed. Read only in `manual` mode; in the other two it is ignored rather than mixed in.

programmeTask.title: Programme task
programmeTask.description: One task under one programme. Its own record, because a programme's plan is not a case and does not belong on one.

status.title: Status
status.description: Where the task stands. `fromTasks` progress counts closed over all.

cycle.title: Cycle
cycle.description: The time box it is in, when it is in one.

programmeTeamMember.title: Programme team member
programmeTeamMember.description: One person in one role on one programme.

role.title: Role
role.description: What they do on it. The same vocabulary the per-role estimates use.

programmeWorkItem.title: Programme work item
programmeWorkItem.description: A piece of work owned by any app, hanging under a programme by reference. The referenced object is never copied, and deleting a programme deletes its references and nothing else. One work item belongs to at most ONE programme, so effort and progress roll up unambiguously.

domainObjectType.title: Object type
domainObjectType.description: The `<app>:<schema>` literal of the referenced object, for example dossiq:zaak or pipelinq:lead. Opaque: pipelinq does not parse it and does not require the app to be installed.

title.title: Title
title.description: The referenced object's title as it read when the link was made. A fallback for rendering, NOT the source of truth: when the owning app is present its own title wins, and when it is absent this is what keeps the item visible as unresolved rather than hidden.

estimationScale.title: Estimation scale
estimationScale.description: An ordered set of estimate points with a label and a numeric weight. At most one scale is active per scope; a second activation in one scope is refused. A scale set inactive keeps resolving on estimates already written, so a historic figure keeps its meaning.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: `instance`, or an org unit id. One active scale per scope.

label.title: Label
label.description: What an estimator picks, for example 1, 2, 3, 5, 8.

weight.title: Weight
weight.description: What it counts for when totalling.

active.title: Active
active.description: Whether new estimates may be written on it.

programmeEstimate.title: Programme estimate
programmeEstimate.description: One role's estimate of one work item, on the active scale. A work item carries one estimate per role, and the total is DERIVED on read as the sum of the parts. No total is stored: a stored total drifts from its parts the first time one changes, silently.

role.title: Role
role.description: Whose effort this estimates, for example juridisch or vakafdeling. A bezwaar costs both, and today both are one number.

point.title: Point
point.description: The point's label on the scale.

scale.title: Scale
scale.description: The scale the point was picked from, recorded so a retired scale still resolves this estimate's meaning.

programmeCycle.title: Programme cycle
programmeCycle.description: A named time box under a programme. Closing it writes a versioned progress snapshot, and a chart of a closed cycle reads the snapshot, so a later edit to the work beneath it cannot rewrite what the chart showed. The live figures stay readable beside it.

snapshots.title: Snapshots
snapshots.description: One entry per close, each with its own version. Reopening and closing again appends rather than overwrites, so two closes leave two snapshots and neither is lost.

version.title: Version
version.description: 1 for the first close, 2 for the next.

total.title: Total
total.description: Items in the cycle as they stood.
